text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> P1: Usage / metering pipeline lag detected for billing-service. Policy: billing-eng -> eng-oncall. Runbook: /runbooks/billing-metering-lag. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PAG12345

pagerduty-bot: Notification sent to escalation policy. Escalation step 1: bob (oncall).

bob (oncall): ack. jumping in. initial check: consumer group `billing-meter-consumer` lagging, retention queue growing. I'll pull consumer lag metrics.

alice (billing-eng): noted. seeing high consumer lag on partition 7. last processed offset stopped ~1712000. tokens/sec dropped from ~150k to ~2k. looks like downstream write errors to metering-db started at 23:01 UTC.

carla (support-l2): heads up — CS already has two customers flagged: invoice 98765 and 99210 reported missing token counts. both on weekly billing. they're blocked from invoicing.

bob (oncall): running quick checks now. kubectl logs -n billing deployment/ingestion-consumer | tail -n 200 -> seeing repeated DB timeout errors.

bob (oncall): ```
2024-07-18T23:03:12Z ERROR write_to_metering_db timeout after 10s (retry 3/5)
2024-07-18T23:03:18Z WARN consumer commit failed: write error
2024-07-18T23:05:01Z INFO processed 10 records in 1s
```

alice (billing-eng): DB intermittent timeouts coincide with a large spike in background maintenance on metering-db-host-2. Ops ran a compaction job ~22:58 UTC. Might be saturating I/O.

emma (payments): if writes are failing, token counts won't be recorded. that explains missing tokens on those invoices. we need either to resume writes or compute deltas from consumer backlog for manual invoicing.

david (customer-success): assigning me to coordinate customer comms. I'll draft a short message to affected accounts saying we detected a metering ingestion lag and are working on catch-up; ETA TBD. Can we give an estimate of when data will be reconciled?

bob (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale ingestion-consumer replicas x2, 2) throttle compaction on metering-db-host-2 or move it off, 3) enable temporary write-retry-backoff to avoid flooding DB. Doing step 1 now: `kubectl scale deploy/ingestion-consumer --replicas=6 -n billing`

bob (oncall): scaling done, replicas coming up. monitoring lag.

alice (billing-eng): I'm going to open a quick DB ticket to pause compaction and move to off-peak. pinging eng-db. If compaction is the culprit, that should reduce I/O and let writes resume.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation step 2 triggered: paging alice (billing-eng) -> ack required.

alice (billing-eng): ack. on it. contacting eng-db.

carla (support-l2): @david I'm pasting customer IDs: acct-5561 (invoice 98765), acct-2234 (invoice 99210). both are high-usage customers. they will want ETA.

david (customer-success): thanks. I'll prepare comms but will wait for an ETA.

bob (oncall): after scaling, consumer throughput improved to ~110k tokens/min, still below baseline. backlog length decreasing slowly. Writing to DB still sporadic; retries still visible.

alice (billing-eng): eng-db responded: compaction paused on metering-db-host-2, moved off-peak. DB I/O dropped ~70%. they suggest a rolling restart of ingestion-writers to reconnect pools.

bob (oncall): planning a rolling restart of deployment/billing-writer to clear any stale DB connections. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/billing-writer -n billing` — executing now.

bob (oncall): restart done. verifying writes...

bob (oncall): good signal: write success rate back to normal for new events. backlog processing rate jumped to 180k tokens/min. looks like most writes are catching up.

emma (payments): if backlog finishes within a few hours we can avoid manual invoicing. what's ETA estimate?

alice (billing-eng): with current rate, backlog should be cleared in ~1.5 hours. but we need to watch for any repeat DB pressure.

david (customer-success): thanks — I'll message affected customers with that ETA and say we're doing backfill and will confirm when invoices are finalized.

carla (support-l2): logged incident ticket for customers and set status -> investigating.

bob (oncall): I'll keep monitoring for 30m then start a handoff. My shift ends in ~25m. If stable, I'll hand off to emma.

pagerduty-bot: Alert status changed -> Acknowledged by bob (oncall).

alice (billing-eng): follow-up: we should add a circuit-breaker for compaction overlap with high-ingestion windows and add DB slow-query alarms to prevent silent saturation. Filing a postmortem action item.

emma (payments): I'll take over monitoring if bob needs to go. please @mention me for any regression.

bob (oncall): handing off now to emma. summary: DB compaction caused write timeouts -> consumer lag -> invoice-blocking risk. scaling and pausing compaction restored writes; backlog processing at 180k tokens/min, estimated catch-up 1.5h. watchers: alice/emma.

emma (payments): ack. picked up. will monitor until backlog < 5k msgs and confirm.

david (customer-success): sent update to affected customers with ETA 90m and offered manual reconciliation if needed sooner.

carla (support-l2): marked customers notified (notes: acct-5561 acct-2234).

bob (oncall): leaving final note: I'll file an incident on ops board with timeline + RCA draft. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident auto-close candidate scheduled if no further pages in 2h.
